messages:
support-sarah: Heads-up — AcmeMaps on prod reported a sharp p99 jump for /v1/generate around 21:04 UTC. p95 stayed ~230ms but p99 spiked to ~2.6s. They say it happens during short-burst patterns (many tiny requests). They attached a request timeline and customer traces.

alex: thx. can you paste the trace + any batch logs? is this only for their key or across multiple customers?

support-sarah: only their API key so far. trace link: https://traces.internal/r/abc123 (linked span shows long wait before first token returned). Attach: sample logs from the node handling their requests.

maria: copying logs extracts here. looks like continuous-batcher held requests waiting for batch completion and late arrivals triggered large wait times.

maria: ```
[2026-03-14T21:03:59.123Z] batcher.INFO batch_id=0x1f created size=1 target_size=16 hold_ms=50 waited_ms=4200 flush=timeout reason=late_arrival\n
[2026-03-14T21:04:03.547Z] batcher.INFO batch_id=0x1f flush assembled_size=3 latency_ms=2600 kvcache_hits=0\n
[2026-03-14T21:04:03.548Z] runtime.DEBUG infer_start batch_id=0x1f seq_len=24\n
```

alex: so hold_ms is 50ms but we're seeing waits of multiple seconds. looks like rare late arrival bursts where a few requests trickle in and keep the batch open. is partial_flush enabled? any customer-specific policy?

maria: partial_flush=false for this pool. max_batch_size=16. routing policy is default. the arrival pattern from AcmeMaps is high variance: lots of tiny requests with random jitter.

sam: this rings a bell — continuous batching tradeoff: if you use a small hold window and large target batch size without partial flush, tail latency can blow up when arrival rate is borderline. small batches sit waiting for more arrivals until they hit the hold deadline, but if late arrivals keep extending it (edge case of our batching state machine), you get multi-second waits. I have a repro script.

sam: repro steps (quick):
```
# Python script that sends Poisson bursts of tiny requests with jitter
python3 scripts/repro_burst.py --rate 120 --burst-size 1-5 --jitter 0.2 --duration 60 --url https://api.internal/v1/generate --key <acme-key>
```

sam: or try wrk with a custom Lua to emulate many short requests + random sleeps:
```
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60 --latency --script=burst.lua https://api.internal/v1/generate
```

sam: burst.lua (very small snippet):
```
wrk.method = "POST"
wrk.body = '{"input":"hi"}'
function init() end
function request()
  if math.random() < 0.1 then
    -- occasional longer pause to create late arrival
    socket.sleep(0.05)
  end
  return wrk.format(nil, "/v1/generate", nil, wrk.body)
end
```

alex: good repro. what's the quick mitigation we can apply without a full rollout?

maria: immediate mitigations we can safely try (canary):
- enable partial_flush=true so batches flush early when threshold reached
- reduce hold_ms from 50 -> 5 (aggressive low-latency) for the low-latency pool
- add early_flush_threshold=0.6 (flush when 60% of target size) to avoid hold loops
- route AcmeMaps to low-latency pool with smaller batching config (also temporarily increase CPU capacity)

kevin: customer impact? smaller batches -> higher cost per token but lower p99. AcmeMaps agreed to trial a low-latency mode if we can make it reversible quickly.

maria: proposed canary plan:
1) create a canary pool tag "ll-1" with partial_flush=true, hold_ms=5, max_batch_size=32, early_flush_threshold=0.6
2) enable for 2 hosts in prod in region us-west-2
3) route AcmeMaps key to ll-1 for the canary window
4) monitor p50/p95/p99, tok/sec, and CPU; observe for 15 minutes
5) if p99 drops and cost delta acceptable, roll to more hosts; else rollback and collect traces

alex: metrics to watch: inference_latency_p99, batch_wait_time_p99, avg_batch_size, token_cost_per_minute, host_cpu. set alerts for batch_wait_time_p99 > 800ms or avg_batch_size drop < 1.2 (indicates flapping)

ops-bot: deploy request queued: deploy-batcher-config(ll-1) -> canary-2hosts. CI checks passed.

maria: sample config snippet to apply in rollout:
```
continuous_batcher:
  pool: ll-1
  hold_ms: 5
  max_batch_size: 32
  target_batch_size: 16
  partial_flush: true
  early_flush_threshold: 0.6
  stats_interval_ms: 1000
```

sam: I'll add the repro harness to infra-tests and include the wrk Lua. also adding a test that simulates poisson arrival to catch this in CI.

alex: escalation communications — I'll ping AcmeMaps with ETA and ask them to keep us in the loop. Sarah, can you share the canary window and rollback instructions with them?

support-sarah: on it. will message them and add them to the incident thread. also requested their synthetic logs for the last 6 hours.

maria: after canary we should consider longer-term fixes: smarter adaptive batching (auto-adjust hold_ms based on current arrival rate), per-key routing heuristics, or a QoS lane for low-latency customers. Also we should harden the batching state machine so late-arrival logic cannot extend waits beyond X seconds (safety cap).

kevin: prioritize adaptive batching work on roadmap? this repeats across a few mid-market customers.

alex: agree. for now let's run the canary and wake the on-call if p99 > 1s for >5 minutes. maria owns rollout, sam owns repro/test, alex will coordinate customer comms. I'll update this thread with status.

support-sarah: canary rolling now to 2 hosts (deploy id: deploy-ll-20260314-01). will report back in ~10m.

ops-bot: canary deployed to hosts host-12, host-13. health checks passing.

maria: initial numbers after 5m: p99 for AcmeMaps dropped from 2.6s -> 180ms on canary pool. avg_batch_size down from 1.7 -> 1.3. CPU per-host up ~8%.

alex: excellent. keep monitoring. if stable at 15m we can expand to 10 hosts.

support-sarah: customer confirmed improved UX. closing loop asking for confirmation after 24h. assigning followups in tracker: SRE-1198.

maria: filing a small postmortem and action items: (1) backport partial_flush safe defaults to prod pools, (2) add safety cap to batch wait, (3) schedule adaptive-batching spike in Q2.

alex: thanks everyone. leaving thread open until postmortem linked.\n
